step5_identityAndIdempotencyDesign.tenantAxis: companyId - a real Company row, standard tenant scoping identical to every other model in this schema.

documentVersionAxis.mechanism: packageKey = computeAnalysisPackageKey(companyId, documentIds) = a content-derived hash of this run's own SORTED, de-duplicated document-id set (lib/contract-model/analysis/identity.ts, reusing lib/contract-model/compiler/hashing.ts's own hashParts primitive verbatim - never a second hashing convention).
documentVersionAxis.whyDocumentIdAloneIsAValidContentProxy: Document rows in this codebase are immutable once created: lib/connectors/upload-connector.ts's own uploadDocumentThroughIngestion computes a real content hash BEFORE storage and converges byte-identical re-uploads onto the EXISTING Document row (never creating a second one, never mutating the first) - independently confirmed by reading that file's own dedup contract and its own concurrency-safe unwind-the-loser logic. No code path anywhere in this repository mutates an existing Document row's own stored bytes in place (grep-confirmed: zero writers of `storageRef` after Document.create). A document's id is therefore already a safe, sufficient, and MUCH cheaper proxy for 'this exact content' than re-hashing every document's full text on every run.
documentVersionAxis.consequence: Adding a genuinely NEW document to the analyzed set changes the sorted id list and therefore packageKey - a distinct AnalysisRun identity, satisfying 'a new document version runs independently.' Re-running over the IDENTICAL document set always re-derives the SAME packageKey, converging on the SAME AnalysisRun row.

step5_identityAndIdempotencyDesign.algorithmVersionAxis: analysisAlgorithmVersion = CONTRACT_ANALYSIS_ORCHESTRATOR_VERSION (lib/contract-model/analysis/identity.ts) - a constant this orchestration file's own maintainer bumps whenever the COMPOSED SEQUENCE itself changes (a stage added/removed/reordered), deliberately NOT bumped for a change confined entirely inside one of the already-independently-versioned sub-modules (STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION, DISCOVERY_RUN_VERSION, SEMANTIC_COMPILER_ALGORITHM_VERSION, SEMANTIC_VERIFIER_ALGORITHM_VERSION, SEMANTIC_COVERAGE_ALGORITHM_VERSION each already own their own internal versioning independently).
step5_identityAndIdempotencyDesign.concurrencyGuard: startOrResumeAnalysisRun (lib/contract-model/analysis/service.ts) treats an existing RUNNING row younger than STALE_RUNNING_THRESHOLD_MS (30 minutes) as an active, in-flight run and returns SKIPPED_ALREADY_RUNNING rather than starting a second concurrent execution for the identical identity. An OLDER RUNNING row (the owning process crashed/was killed mid-run) is treated as abandoned and safely re-entered - safe by construction because every downstream write this run's own body performs (persistStructuralNodes, persistPackageGraph, recordClaimReview) is independently idempotent (upsert-by-stableKey or upsert-by-claimKey; see each module's own persistence-layer header comments), so re-running from the top after a crash never duplicates state, it only redoes deterministic/cheap work and re-upserts already-upserted rows.

casesProvedAgainstRealPostgres.proof: Two full runContractAnalysis calls over the identical document set resolve to the SAME AnalysisRun.id, exactly one AnalysisRun row exists afterward, and the resulting ClaimReviewItem row ids are byte-identical before/after (updated in place, never duplicated).
Uploading a second, genuinely new document and re-running changes packageKey and produces a SECOND, independent AnalysisRun row (2 total) with documentIds.length === 2.

A row inserted under the identical (companyId, packageKey) but a DIFFERENT analysisAlgorithmVersion coexists as a genuinely separate row under the schema's own @@unique constraint - proving a version bump is structurally guaranteed to cause independent reprocessing, not merely asserted by convention.
A pre-existing, fresh RUNNING row for the identical identity causes a new runContractAnalysis call to return SKIPPED_ALREADY_RUNNING without starting a second execution or creating a second row.
A company with zero contract-shaped documents produces a real, honest no-op outcome and creates zero AnalysisRun rows - never a fabricated/placeholder run record.

A Document row lacking a storageRef (cannot be re-parsed) causes the whole run to route to a persisted FAILED AnalysisRun with a real fatalError payload, rather than a silent partial success or an uncaught exception.
